title: On exact randomization-based covariate-adjusted confidence intervals
headline: Open finding: the stated monotonicity condition does not guarantee nominal coverage of the paper's single-interval ANCOVA root-sorting procedure.

work.title: On exact randomization-based covariate-adjusted confidence intervals

claims.label: Section 3.2 Theorem 1 coverage guarantee
claims.gist: The displayed condition is used to justify a monotone p-value path and a single interval formed by sorting crossing roots.
claims.statement: Theorem 1's displayed condition is sufficient to justify the root-sorting confidence interval and its nominal finite-sample coverage.
conditions: Complete randomization with a sharp constant treatment effect.
ANCOVA residualization on an intercept and fixed covariates.
The displayed Theorem 1 condition is positive for every assignment.
claims.quantifiers: The coverage guarantee is presented for experiments satisfying the stated condition; the finite witness below satisfies it for all 70 four-of-eight assignments.

result.summary: An exact eight-unit complete-randomization example satisfies the stated condition for every assignment, yet the printed fifth-root 95% interval covers the true sharp effect in only 60 of 70 assignments.
result.witness: With x=(1,-1,0,1,-6,-5,-3,-5), sharp-null outcomes (-1,2,2,0,5,1,-5,3), and four treated units, the minimum displayed-condition value across all 70 assignments is 12/23>0. For the observed assignment (1,0,1,1,0,0,1,0), the printed interval is [-2869/340,-1305/731], excluding the true effect 0, while the exact Fisher p-value at 0 is 2/35.
result.argument: The theorem's own monotonicity calculation concerns the shift Y+theta(2q-1), for which the displayed condition simplifies to 2 r_q' r_q>0 whenever the ANCOVA coefficient is identified. The Fisher inversion used by the interval instead follows Y+theta(q-z). Its slope can be negative; in the witness one candidate assignment has slope -1/2. The actual p-value function therefore need not be monotone. Direct inversion gives a disconnected, unbounded acceptance set, so one interval formed from two sorted roots cannot represent it.
not_claimed: Fisher randomization p-values are not exact.
Theorem 1's algebraic monotonicity statement along its own displayed shift is false.
A full inversion that reconstructs the non-monotone p-value function is invalid.
result.repair_note: A root-sorting shortcut needs a condition on the actual imputation-path slopes; alternatively, retain all p-value jumps and invert the full non-monotone function.

vor_check.detail: The publisher article text and decisive theorem/algorithm wording were checked. Source verification remains partial because the publisher PDF bytes and supplementary material were not both available through the source-lock workflow.

evidence.detail: A fresh hostile validation reproduced the exact 70-assignment enumeration, the root-sorting undercoverage, the true-null Fisher p-value, the disconnected exact inversion, and the distinction between the theorem path and the algorithm's imputation path.
